resolutions.researcher_notes: Both current refs (a Facebook post and this same sirtggp.com URL) were DEAD/unverifiable via automated check; re-verified sirtggp.com manually -- it passes url_verifier (200, contains expected Arabic text) and I independently read the page: Sirt Gulf Gas Projects Co. (a Libyan national pipeline-services contractor, est. 2007) dated a 2020-02-11 contract to pig/clean the 'Entessar-Sarir' 20-inch pipeline (114 km) -- routine maintenance on a named, in-service line is strong evidence it was actually operating by 2020. Second, independent origin: Waha Oil Company's own site (wahaoil.ly, archived via Wayback since the live site now 403s bots), dated 2021-01-04, titled 'Resumption of normal feed to the Sarir station line' -- describes completing compressor maintenance ahead of schedule and restarting full-capacity gas supply to 'khat haql al-Intisar (A) wa mahattat al-Sarir' (the Intisar(A) field-to-Sarir-station line), explicitly to keep gas reaching the electricity grid, and references an upcoming 'phase 2'. Two independent sources (a pipeline-services contractor vs. the operator itself), both post-dating and superseding GEM's own wiki page, which candidly states 'There is no direct evidence that the pipeline is operating, but this is the presumed status given an agreement that occurred in 2017' -- i.e. GEM's own basis for Status was already flagged as weak. These two sources upgrade Status=operating from presumed to well-evidenced, tier high. CAVEAT: the pipeline evidently sat unfinished/stalled 2014-2017 (see Start/Construction below) before entering service, so 'operating' should not be read as continuous since an early start date.

eanlibya.com (2017-07-22) repeatedly calls this 'khat naql al-ghaz' (gas transmission line) feeding 'mahattat al-Sarir al-ghaziyah' (the Sarir GAS power station). wahaoil.ly (2021-01-04, read via Wayback) independently confirms: the incident involved a compressor/gas-plant fault, and restoring 'gas' ('al-ghaz') supply to the same Intisar(A)-Sarir line so it keeps reaching the electricity network. Two independent, unambiguous confirmations of Fuel=Gas.

The only source tying this pipeline to 2014 is eanlibya.com (2017-07-22), which says the Petrojet-built project 'had been stopped since 2014' ('الذي توقف منذ سنة 2014') -- i.e. 2014 is when construction work HALTED, not when it began. I found no source giving an actual construction-START year (OPEC's ASB2012, which covers 2011 data, has NO 'Intisar/Sarir' or 'Intesar/Sarir' entry in either its gas-pipeline (Table 4.10) or crude-pipeline (Table 4.9) Libya listings -- checked via a recovered Wayback capture + pdftotext -- consistent with this line not yet existing/being under construction as of 2011, but that's a negative inference, not a positive construction-year source). Left UNRESOLVED rather than pair a ref that would misrepresent what it actually supports (a halt date, not a start date) -- flagging that GEM's ConstructionYear=2014 likely conflates 'construction paused' with 'construction began' and should be reviewed.

This is the article gem.wiki itself already cites for Start, and it is the only source found tying the pipeline to 2017 -- but it reports a 2017-07-20 Presidential Council meeting (chaired by advisor Miloud Al-Rajbani, with contractor Petrojet and consultant Brand/Omar Al-Abdiyah) agreeing to set up a mechanism to resume and complete the stalled line 'during the upcoming month of August' 2017 -- an AGREEMENT to resume/finish construction, not a confirmed in-service/start date. Restoring this ref preserves traceability for the existing value (and matches gem.wiki's own hedge that 2017 is merely 'presumed'), but tier is low: it's a single source and describes the wrong milestone (resume-agreement, not verified operational start). The 2020 (sirtggp) and 2021 (Waha) sources under Status show the line was demonstrably in service by 2020 at the latest -- StartYear1 could plausibly be anywhere 2017-2020 and this pass could not narrow it further.

VALUE CONTRADICTION, not just unsourced: the only length-bearing source found for this exact named line -- sirtggp.com's 2020 pigging-contract page, titled '...20-inch Intisar-Sarir pipeline, 114 km' ('...20 بوصة على بعد 114 كم') -- states 114 km, roughly HALF of GEM's recorded 235.00 km. Diameter (20 in) and route name match GEM exactly, so this isn't a different pipeline; it's a specific, dated, diameter-matching source directly disagreeing with the sheet's length. Did not find any source supporting 235 km specifically (searched English and Arabic; checked OPEC ASB2012, which has no Intisar/Sarir entry at all -- see Construction notes). Left UNRESOLVED rather than cite a source that contradicts the stated value -- flagging for the human editor to reconcile 235 km vs. the sourced 114 km (possible explanations: a longer routing/right-of-way distance vs. sirtggp's as-built pipe length, a since-superseded design length, or GEM's 235 km being in error).

Three independent sources all name the same route: sirtggp.com and eanlibya.com both call it 'Intisar-Sarir' ('إنتصار-السرير'); wahaoil.ly (Wayback) calls it 'khat haql al-Intisar (A) wa mahattat al-Sarir' (the Intisar(A) field / Sarir station line). Consistent with Start=Intisar Oil field (Sirte Basin) and End=Sarir field (Cyrenaica). Note the sources consistently describe the Sarir end as 'mahattat al-Sarir' (Sarir STATION/plant, i.e. the gas-fired power/gathering station at Sarir), not literally 'Sarir oil field' -- same location, but EndLocation could be tightened to 'Sarir gas station' if more precision is wanted; not flagging as a contradiction, just a naming-precision note.

wahaoil.ly's own 2021-01-04 post (Wayback) describes Waha Oil Company's own engineering/operations teams at Al-Fareg field restoring gas supply/compression into this exact Intisar(A)-Sarir line -- a specific, direct match. Second, independent origin: NOC's own official affiliated-companies page (noc.ly, verified live) lists Waha Oil Company as an NOC affiliate, with the Arabic name شركة الواحة للنفط matching the brief's Operator value verbatim -- confirms Waha Oil Co. is a real, NOC-recognized operating entity (general corroboration of identity, not route-specific). Tier high on the strength of the route-specific self-report plus the independent corporate-identity confirmation. NOTE: a companion deep-sweep pass on this same row flagged that the TRANSMISSION PIPELINE ASSET itself may be attributed by other sources (sirtggp.com's pigging-contract page) to a different, state-owned entity ('al-Sharikah al-'Ammah li-Naql wa Tawzi' al-Ghaz' / General Company for Gas Transport and Distribution) rather than Waha -- see Owner notes. That doesn't contradict Operator=Waha Oil Co. (Waha's own site clearly describes running gas supply/compression INTO this line from its own field operations), but the two facts (who feeds gas into the line vs. who legally owns/operates the transmission pipe) may need to be reconciled by a human editor if GEM's schema distinguishes them.

Owner percentages (NOC 59.18%, ConocoPhillips 16.33%, TotalEnergies 16.33%, Hess 8.16%) match EXACTLY, verbatim, a Total S.A. SEC filing: EX-99.5 to a Form 6-K (accession 0001193125-19-326321), an official Total press release dated 10 Dec 2019, stating 'The NOC (59.18%), Total (16.33%), ConocoPhillips (16.33%) and Hess (8.16%) jointly own the Waha concessions.' url_verifier reports HTTP 403 on the live sec.gov URL because SEC blocks the tool's default User-Agent as an undeclared bot (documented false-negative pattern, also hit by a companion shard, P1861/Farigh-Intesar, on this same source) -- manually re-fetched with a declared UA and confirmed HTTP 200 with the exact '59.18%...16.33%...16.33%...8.16%' string present. Second, independent origin: Marathon Oil Corp's FY2018 Form 10-K (accession 0000101778-19-000022) states it sold its 16.33% non-operated Waha-concession interest to a Total S.A. subsidiary -- independently corroborates the Total/ex-Marathon 16.33% stake from the seller's side (cited via a Wayback capture that passes url_verifier directly). CAVEAT (important, carried over from a companion deep-sweep pass on this row): this percentage split is well-established as the ownership of the WAHA OIL CONCESSION/FIELDS -- but two other independent Arabic sources (eanlibya.com 2017 and sirtggp.com 2020) instead name a different entity, 'al-Sharikah al-'Ammah li-Naql wa Tawzi' al-Ghaz' (General Company for Gas Transport and Distribution), as the party that negotiated/owns the TRANSMISSION PIPELINE ASSET itself (with Petrojet as EPC contractor). I could not find a source that ties the Waha consortium percentages specifically to ownership of this pipeline (as opposed to the upstream field/concession) -- so while the cited SEC sources correctly and strongly support the NUMBERS as GEM has recorded them (and match a sibling row's, P1861's, reusable Owner reference for any Waha-concession pipeline), a human editor should decide whether Owner for THIS specific transmission-pipeline row should instead read General Company for Gas Transport and Distribution. Flagging as a genuine attribution question rather than asserting GEM is wrong.

P3987 (Intisar-Sarir) and P3988 (Fargh-Sarir) read as TWO DISTINCT physical lines, not a double-count, though both feed the same Sarir hub and their names/histories are easy to conflate. Evidence they are separate assets: (1) different named source fields -- Intisar (Sirte Basin concession-103 field) vs. Fargh/Faregh (a different, separately-named Waha field) -- feeding the same downstream Sarir station; (2) different specs in independent, dated source documents -- sirtggp.com's 2020 contract page gives Intisar-Sarir as 20-inch / 114 km, while Waha Oil's own 2020-11-23 news post (cited in the P3988 shard) gives Fargh-Sarir as 97 km, explicitly calling it 'khat al-Fargh-Sarir' (the Fargh-Sarir line) as its own named project, separate from the Intisar line; (3) GEM's own recorded lengths for the two rows (235 km vs 97 km) are far enough apart, and the two independently-sourced values I found (114 km for Intisar-Sarir vs. 97 km for Fargh-Sarir) are also clearly distinct, that this isn't the same segment measured two ways. I did not find a single source describing 'Intisar-Sarir' and 'Fargh-Sarir' as alternate names for one project; every source treats them as separate lines within the same Sirte-Basin-to-Sarir gas-gathering scheme (also distinct from P1861 Farigh-Intesar/Waha-Faregh's OPEC-sourced 110 mi / 177 km line, which runs the other direction, Faregh TO Intesar, not to Sarir). Net read: not a redundancy, but part of a genuinely multi-line network around Intisar/Fargh/Sarir that is easy to mis-merge -- worth a note in country docs that these are parallel/sequential feeder lines, not duplicate records of one pipeline. Also unrelated: a brand-new (April 2026) 42-inch, 130 km 'Intisar A/103-Brega' pipeline just entered trial operation per NOC/Libya Observer/Pipeline Technology Journal reporting -- confirmed via WebFetch this is a DIFFERENT route (different diameter, length, and destination -- Brega, not Sarir) and not a duplicate or update candidate for P3987/P3988; flagging only so it isn't mistaken for this pipeline in later research.
